data.narrative:
Tokamak Energy, a Series C nuclear energy company that has raised $335M+, is valued within a frontier-tech sector represented by 3 public comparables (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Antares. The nuclear energy peer universe remains nascent and heterogeneous, limiting direct statistical comparison.

A single applicable valuation method—stage progression—anchors this analysis. Using total capital raised ($335M) as a baseline proxy and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement yields an implied valuation of $570M. This reflects the funding-to-valuation conversion expected at this stage of company maturity. A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the nuclear energy sector; no subset of three or more directly comparable datapoints exists at Tokamak's valuation tier and development phase.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $484M to $655M, centered on $570M. Key uncertainties include the appropriate discount or premium relative to public nuclear energy trading multiples, the liquidity and stage-readiness profile of private peers, and the technical and regulatory risks inherent to pre-commercial nuclear platforms. The single-method triangulation reflects genuine data scarcity rather than convergence and should be viewed as a narrow anchoring point pending additional comparable transactions.
